# istqb-ai-ready

> QA knowledge base structured for AI tools, built from the ISTQB® CTFL Syllabus v4.0.1.
> Each syllabus section has a file with frontmatter, our own summary and the original PDF page; the full text exists only locally in syllabus-text/.

Read CLAUDE.md first (usage rules). Always cite the section used, e.g. "per syllabus 4.2.1".
syllabus/ holds the shells (our summaries). If syllabus-text/<same path> exists, it has the official text of the section.

## Rules and notice

- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): how an AI should query and cite this base
- [LEGAL-NOTICE.md](LEGAL-NOTICE.md): attribution to ISTQB® and conditions of use
- [README.md](README.md): what this is, how to regenerate it from the PDF, how to use it in other projects (Portuguese: README.pt-BR.md)

## Practical guides (our interpretation, not the syllabus)

- [guides/black-box-techniques.md](guides/black-box-techniques.md): Black-box techniques in practice (based on 4.1, 4.2, 4.2.1, 4.2.2, 4.2.3, 4.2.4, 4.4.1, 4.5.2, 5.1.5)
- [guides/test-plan-template.md](guides/test-plan-template.md): Test plan template (based on 5.1.1, 5.1.3, 5.1.4, 5.2, 5.3.2, 5.5, 2.2.1, 2.2.2)
- [guides/test-planning-checklist.md](guides/test-planning-checklist.md): Test planning checklist (based on 1.4.1, 1.4.2, 2.1.5, 2.2.1, 2.2.2, 5.1.1, 5.1.2, 5.1.3, 5.1.4, 5.1.5, 5.1.6, 5.1.7, 5.2.2, 5.2.3, 5.2.4, 5.3.1, 5.3.2, 5.4, 5.5)

## Data

- [data/objectives.json](data/objectives.json): the 64 learning objectives (code, K-level, section, file)
- [data/keywords.json](data/keywords.json): keywords of each chapter
- [data/glossary.json](data/glossary.json): syllabus terms with sections and pages; definitions are in the official ISTQB glossary
- [data/summaries.yaml](data/summaries.yaml): our summary of each section (source of the shells)

## Syllabus (shells)

### Introduction

- [0 Introduction](syllabus/00-introduction.md): Why the syllabus exists, who it is for, K-levels, the exam and how the chapters are laid out.

### Chapter 1: Fundamentals of Testing

- [1 Fundamentals of Testing](syllabus/01-fundamentals-of-testing/_index.md): Fundamentals: what testing is, why it matters, the 7 principles, process, testware, roles and skills.
- [1.1 What is Testing?](syllabus/01-fundamentals-of-testing/1.1-what-is-testing.md): Testing as a set of activities to find defects and assess quality, covering verification and validation.
  - [1.1.1 Test Objectives](syllabus/01-fundamentals-of-testing/1.1.1-test-objectives.md) [K1]: Typical test objectives and how context shifts them.
  - [1.1.2 Testing and Debugging](syllabus/01-fundamentals-of-testing/1.1.2-testing-and-debugging.md) [K2]: Testing and debugging are separate activities.
- [1.2 Why is Testing Necessary?](syllabus/01-fundamentals-of-testing/1.2-why-is-testing-necessary.md): Testing as quality control, which any stakeholder can contribute to.
  - [1.2.1 Testing’s Contributions to Success](syllabus/01-fundamentals-of-testing/1.2.1-testings-contributions-to-success.md) [K2]: How testing contributes to project success.
  - [1.2.2 Testing and Quality Assurance (QA)](syllabus/01-fundamentals-of-testing/1.2.2-testing-and-quality-assurance-qa.md) [K1]: Testing (product-focused control) vs QA (process-focused assurance).
  - [1.2.3 Errors, Defects, Failures, and Root Causes](syllabus/01-fundamentals-of-testing/1.2.3-errors-defects-failures-and-root-causes.md) [K2]: The error → defect → failure chain and the idea of root cause.
- [1.3 Testing Principles](syllabus/01-fundamentals-of-testing/1.3-testing-principles.md) [K2]: The seven testing principles.
- [1.4 Test Activities, Testware and Test Roles](syllabus/01-fundamentals-of-testing/1.4-test-activities-testware-and-test-roles.md): The test process: activities, testware and roles, tailored to the context.
  - [1.4.1 Test Activities and Tasks](syllabus/01-fundamentals-of-testing/1.4.1-test-activities-and-tasks.md) [K2]: The seven test activities, from planning to completion.
  - [1.4.2 Test Process in Context](syllabus/01-fundamentals-of-testing/1.4.2-test-process-in-context.md) [K2]: Context factors that shape the test process.
  - [1.4.3 Testware](syllabus/01-fundamentals-of-testing/1.4.3-testware.md) [K2]: Work products (testware) produced by each test activity.
  - [1.4.4 Traceability between the Test Basis and Testware](syllabus/01-fundamentals-of-testing/1.4.4-traceability-between-the-test-basis-and-testware.md) [K2]: Traceability between test basis, testware, results and defects.
  - [1.4.5 Roles in Testing](syllabus/01-fundamentals-of-testing/1.4.5-roles-in-testing.md) [K2]: The two main roles: test management and testing.
- [1.5 Essential Skills and Good Practices in Testing](syllabus/01-fundamentals-of-testing/1.5-essential-skills-and-good-practices-in-testing.md): Essential tester skills and good practices.
  - [1.5.1 Generic Skills Required for Testing](syllabus/01-fundamentals-of-testing/1.5.1-generic-skills-required-for-testing.md) [K2]: Generic skills relevant to testing, with emphasis on communication.
  - [1.5.2 Whole Team Approach](syllabus/01-fundamentals-of-testing/1.5.2-whole-team-approach.md) [K1]: Whole team approach.
  - [1.5.3 Independence of Testing](syllabus/01-fundamentals-of-testing/1.5.3-independence-of-testing.md) [K2]: Degrees of test independence, with benefits and drawbacks.

### Chapter 2: Testing Throughout the Software Development Lifecycle

- [2 Testing Throughout the Software Development Lifecycle](syllabus/02-testing-throughout-the-software-development-lifecycle/_index.md): Testing across the lifecycle: SDLC models, test-first, DevOps, shift left, levels, types and maintenance.
- [2.1 Testing in the Context of a Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC)](syllabus/02-testing-throughout-the-software-development-lifecycle/2.1-testing-in-the-context-of-a-software-development-lifecycle-sdlc.md): Lifecycle models (sequential, iterative, incremental) and agile methods.
  - [2.1.1 Impact of the Software Development Lifecycle on Testing](syllabus/02-testing-throughout-the-software-development-lifecycle/2.1.1-impact-of-the-software-development-lifecycle-on-testing.md) [K2]: How the choice of SDLC changes testing.
  - [2.1.2 Software Development Lifecycle and Good Testing Practices](syllabus/02-testing-throughout-the-software-development-lifecycle/2.1.2-software-development-lifecycle-and-good-testing-practices.md) [K1]: Good testing practices that hold for any SDLC.
  - [2.1.3 Testing as a Driver for Software Development](syllabus/02-testing-throughout-the-software-development-lifecycle/2.1.3-testing-as-a-driver-for-software-development.md) [K1]: TDD, ATDD and BDD: tests written before code steer development.
  - [2.1.4 DevOps and Testing](syllabus/02-testing-throughout-the-software-development-lifecycle/2.1.4-devops-and-testing.md) [K2]: DevOps and its benefits and risks for testing.
  - [2.1.5 Shift Left](syllabus/02-testing-throughout-the-software-development-lifecycle/2.1.5-shift-left.md) [K2]: Shift left: test earlier, without dropping later testing.
  - [2.1.6 Retrospectives and Process Improvement](syllabus/02-testing-throughout-the-software-development-lifecycle/2.1.6-retrospectives-and-process-improvement.md) [K2]: Retrospectives as a continuous improvement mechanism.
- [2.2 Test Levels and Test Types](syllabus/02-testing-throughout-the-software-development-lifecycle/2.2-test-levels-and-test-types.md): Test levels (when/where) and test types (what).
  - [2.2.1 Test Levels](syllabus/02-testing-throughout-the-software-development-lifecycle/2.2.1-test-levels.md) [K2]: The five levels: component, component integration, system, system integration and acceptance.
  - [2.2.2 Test Types](syllabus/02-testing-throughout-the-software-development-lifecycle/2.2.2-test-types.md) [K2]: The four types: functional, non-functional, black-box and white-box.
  - [2.2.3 Confirmation Testing and Regression Testing](syllabus/02-testing-throughout-the-software-development-lifecycle/2.2.3-confirmation-testing-and-regression-testing.md) [K2]: Confirmation testing (is the defect fixed?) vs regression testing (did the change break something?).
- [2.3 Maintenance Testing](syllabus/02-testing-throughout-the-software-development-lifecycle/2.3-maintenance-testing.md) [K2]: Maintenance testing: scope and triggers (modification, migration, retirement).

### Chapter 3: Static Testing

- [3 Static Testing](syllabus/03-static-testing/_index.md): Static testing: examinable work products, value, difference from dynamic, feedback and the review process.
- [3.1 Static Testing Basics](syllabus/03-static-testing/3.1-static-testing-basics.md): Static testing basics: reviews and static analysis.
  - [3.1.1 Work Products Examinable by Static Testing](syllabus/03-static-testing/3.1.1-work-products-examinable-by-static-testing.md) [K1]: Work products that can (or cannot) go through static testing.
  - [3.1.2 Value of Static Testing](syllabus/03-static-testing/3.1.2-value-of-static-testing.md) [K2]: Why static testing pays off.
  - [3.1.3 Differences between Static Testing and Dynamic Testing](syllabus/03-static-testing/3.1.3-differences-between-static-testing-and-dynamic-testing.md) [K2]: Static vs dynamic testing and the defects each finds best.
- [3.2 Feedback and Review Process](syllabus/03-static-testing/3.2-feedback-and-review-process.md): Stakeholder feedback and the review process.
  - [3.2.1 Benefits of Early and Frequent Stakeholder Feedback](syllabus/03-static-testing/3.2.1-benefits-of-early-and-frequent-stakeholder-feedback.md) [K1]: Benefits of early and frequent stakeholder feedback.
  - [3.2.2 Review Process Activities](syllabus/03-static-testing/3.2.2-review-process-activities.md) [K2]: The five activities of the review process (ISO/IEC 20246).
  - [3.2.3 Roles and Responsibilities in Reviews](syllabus/03-static-testing/3.2.3-roles-and-responsibilities-in-reviews.md) [K1]: Review roles: manager, author, moderator, scribe, reviewer and review leader.
  - [3.2.4 Review Types](syllabus/03-static-testing/3.2.4-review-types.md) [K2]: Review types: informal, walkthrough, technical review and inspection.
  - [3.2.5 Success Factors for Reviews](syllabus/03-static-testing/3.2.5-success-factors-for-reviews.md) [K1]: Success factors for reviews.

### Chapter 4: Test Analysis and Design

- [4 Test Analysis and Design](syllabus/04-test-analysis-and-design/_index.md): Test techniques: black-box, white-box, experience-based and collaborative approaches.
- [4.1 Test Techniques Overview](syllabus/04-test-analysis-and-design/4.1-test-techniques-overview.md) [K2]: Overview and classification of test techniques.
- [4.2 Black-Box Test Techniques](syllabus/04-test-analysis-and-design/4.2-black-box-test-techniques.md): Black-box techniques: EP, BVA, decision tables and state transitions.
  - [4.2.1 Equivalence Partitioning](syllabus/04-test-analysis-and-design/4.2.1-equivalence-partitioning.md) [K3]: Equivalence partitioning and Each Choice coverage.
  - [4.2.2 Boundary Value Analysis](syllabus/04-test-analysis-and-design/4.2.2-boundary-value-analysis.md) [K3]: Boundary value analysis in its 2-value and 3-value forms.
  - [4.2.3 Decision Table Testing](syllabus/04-test-analysis-and-design/4.2.3-decision-table-testing.md) [K3]: Decision table testing for combinations of conditions.
  - [4.2.4 State Transition Testing](syllabus/04-test-analysis-and-design/4.2.4-state-transition-testing.md) [K3]: State transition testing and its three coverage criteria.
- [4.3 White-Box Test Techniques](syllabus/04-test-analysis-and-design/4.3-white-box-test-techniques.md): White-box techniques: statement and branch testing.
  - [4.3.1 Statement Testing and Statement Coverage](syllabus/04-test-analysis-and-design/4.3.1-statement-testing-and-statement-coverage.md) [K2]: Statement testing and statement coverage.
  - [4.3.2 Branch Testing and Branch Coverage](syllabus/04-test-analysis-and-design/4.3.2-branch-testing-and-branch-coverage.md) [K2]: Branch testing and branch coverage; branch subsumes statement.
  - [4.3.3 The Value of White-box Testing](syllabus/04-test-analysis-and-design/4.3.3-the-value-of-white-box-testing.md) [K2]: Value and limits of white-box testing.
- [4.4 Experience-based Test Techniques](syllabus/04-test-analysis-and-design/4.4-experience-based-test-techniques.md): Experience-based techniques: error guessing, exploratory and checklist-based.
  - [4.4.1 Error Guessing](syllabus/04-test-analysis-and-design/4.4.1-error-guessing.md) [K2]: Error guessing and fault attacks.
  - [4.4.2 Exploratory Testing](syllabus/04-test-analysis-and-design/4.4.2-exploratory-testing.md) [K2]: Exploratory and session-based testing (charter, time box, debriefing).
  - [4.4.3 Checklist-Based Testing](syllabus/04-test-analysis-and-design/4.4.3-checklist-based-testing.md) [K2]: Checklist-based testing.
- [4.5 Collaboration-based Test Approaches](syllabus/04-test-analysis-and-design/4.5-collaboration-based-test-approaches.md): Collaborative approaches focused on avoiding defects.
  - [4.5.1 Collaborative User Story Writing](syllabus/04-test-analysis-and-design/4.5.1-collaborative-user-story-writing.md) [K2]: Collaborative user story writing: the 3 C's and INVEST.
  - [4.5.2 Acceptance Criteria](syllabus/04-test-analysis-and-design/4.5.2-acceptance-criteria.md) [K2]: Acceptance criteria: purpose and formats (scenario or rule).
  - [4.5.3 Acceptance Test-driven Development (ATDD)](syllabus/04-test-analysis-and-design/4.5.3-acceptance-test-driven-development-atdd.md) [K3]: ATDD: test cases from acceptance criteria, before implementation.

### Chapter 5: Managing the Test Activities

- [5 Managing the Test Activities](syllabus/05-managing-the-test-activities/_index.md): Test management: planning, estimation, prioritisation, risk, monitoring, reports, configuration and defects.
- [5.1 Test Planning](syllabus/05-managing-the-test-activities/5.1-test-planning.md): Test planning and the tools that support it.
  - [5.1.1 Purpose and Content of a Test Plan](syllabus/05-managing-the-test-activities/5.1.1-purpose-and-content-of-a-test-plan.md) [K2]: Purpose and typical content of a test plan.
  - [5.1.2 Tester's Contribution to Iteration and Release Planning](syllabus/05-managing-the-test-activities/5.1.2-testers-contribution-to-iteration-and-release-planning.md) [K1]: The tester's contribution to release and iteration planning.
  - [5.1.3 Entry Criteria and Exit Criteria](syllabus/05-managing-the-test-activities/5.1.3-entry-criteria-and-exit-criteria.md) [K2]: Entry and exit criteria (Definition of Ready / Definition of Done).
  - [5.1.4 Estimation Techniques](syllabus/05-managing-the-test-activities/5.1.4-estimation-techniques.md) [K3]: Four estimation techniques: ratios, extrapolation, Wideband Delphi and three-point.
  - [5.1.5 Test Case Prioritization](syllabus/05-managing-the-test-activities/5.1.5-test-case-prioritization.md) [K3]: Test case prioritisation: by risk, by coverage and by requirements.
  - [5.1.6 Test Pyramid](syllabus/05-managing-the-test-activities/5.1.6-test-pyramid.md) [K1]: Test pyramid.
  - [5.1.7 Testing Quadrants](syllabus/05-managing-the-test-activities/5.1.7-testing-quadrants.md) [K2]: Marick's testing quadrants (Q1 to Q4).
- [5.2 Risk Management](syllabus/05-managing-the-test-activities/5.2-risk-management.md): Risk management and risk-based testing.
  - [5.2.1 Risk Definition and Risk Attributes](syllabus/05-managing-the-test-activities/5.2.1-risk-definition-and-risk-attributes.md) [K1]: Risk, likelihood, impact and risk level.
  - [5.2.2 Project Risks and Product Risks](syllabus/05-managing-the-test-activities/5.2.2-project-risks-and-product-risks.md) [K2]: Project risks vs product risks.
  - [5.2.3 Product Risk Analysis](syllabus/05-managing-the-test-activities/5.2.3-product-risk-analysis.md) [K2]: Product risk analysis: identification, assessment and use of the results.
  - [5.2.4 Product Risk Control](syllabus/05-managing-the-test-activities/5.2.4-product-risk-control.md) [K2]: Product risk control: mitigation, monitoring and responses.
- [5.3 Test Monitoring, Test Control and Test Completion](syllabus/05-managing-the-test-activities/5.3-test-monitoring-test-control-and-test-completion.md): Test monitoring, test control and test completion.
  - [5.3.1 Metrics used in Testing](syllabus/05-managing-the-test-activities/5.3.1-metrics-used-in-testing.md) [K1]: Metrics used in testing.
  - [5.3.2 Purpose, Content and Audience for Test Reports](syllabus/05-managing-the-test-activities/5.3.2-purpose-content-and-audience-for-test-reports.md) [K2]: Progress report vs completion report: purpose, content and audience.
  - [5.3.3 Communicating the Status of Testing](syllabus/05-managing-the-test-activities/5.3.3-communicating-the-status-of-testing.md) [K2]: Ways to communicate test status.
- [5.4 Configuration Management](syllabus/05-managing-the-test-activities/5.4-configuration-management.md) [K2]: Configuration management in support of testing.
- [5.5 Defect Management](syllabus/05-managing-the-test-activities/5.5-defect-management.md) [K3]: Defect management and the content of a defect report.

### Chapter 6: Test Tools

- [6 Test Tools](syllabus/06-test-tools/_index.md): Test tools: categories and the benefits and risks of automation.
- [6.1 Tool Support for Testing](syllabus/06-test-tools/6.1-tool-support-for-testing.md) [K2]: Categories of tools that support testing.
- [6.2 Benefits and Risks of Test Automation](syllabus/06-test-tools/6.2-benefits-and-risks-of-test-automation.md) [K1]: Benefits and risks of test automation.
